drivers: Recovery balance not provided but ACWR is elevated (z4 zone % jumped from 8% in Aug to 27% in Sep, indicating acute intensity load spike)
Aerobic TE increased from 2.6 (Aug) to 2.9 (Sep), suggesting reduced fatigue resilience
Cadence dropped from 149 (Aug) to 141 (Sep) — consistent with neuromuscular fatigue
Recent long run (10.7 km on 9/6) at 158 bpm and 5.0 aerobic TE — decoupling >5% implies significant aerobic strain
readiness.guidance: The athlete is accumulating fatigue faster than recovery systems can compensate; priority this week is active recovery and load reduction, not performance gains.

monthly_review.summary: September shows a sharp shift toward higher-intensity running with faster paces and elevated HR, but at the cost of efficiency, consistency, and likely sustainability.
monthly_review.highlight: Z4 time surged from 8% in August to 27% in September — a 3.4× increase — while total volume dropped, indicating disproportionate intensity accumulation without sufficient recovery infrastructure.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km would require 12.3 km across just 2 remaining sessions — an unsustainable 6+ km each, likely worsening fatigue. Given compromised readiness, chasing this number is inadvisable and contradicts recovery needs.

insights.title: Z4 dominance without Z1 buffer
insights.body: Z4 zone share jumped from 8% (Aug) to 27% (Sep), while Z1 dropped from 43% to 24% — eliminating the essential low-intensity recovery foundation needed to process high-intensity work.

insights.title: Cadence collapse tracks with aerobic TE rise
insights.body: Cadence fell 8 spm (149 → 141) as aerobic TE rose 0.3 (2.6 → 2.9), suggesting diminished neuromuscular coordination under accumulated strain — a known precursor to inefficient gait and injury risk.

insights.title: Running economy worsened despite faster pace
insights.body: Avg efficiency declined from 14.12 to 14.67 ml/kg/km (+0.55) even as avg pace improved — meaning the runner is expending more oxygen per km at faster speeds, signaling declining aerobic fitness or fatigue-induced inefficiency.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 easy run: 4.5 km, HR ≤128 bpm, cadence ≥145 spm, on Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Restores Z1 volume to rebuild aerobic base and stimulate parasympathetic recovery; cadence target counters recent neuromuscular drift.

recommendations.action: Complete rest or non-weight-bearing activity (e.g., swimming 20 min) on Thursday
recommendations.reason: Zero running load required to allow HRV rebound and reduce cumulative ground contact stress — recent runs show vertical oscillillation rising (6.6 → 8.4) and ground contact increasing (282 → 327 ms).

recommendations.action: Zone 2 tempo progression: 3 × 8 min @ HR 132–136 bpm with 90-sec walk recovery, Friday
recommendations.reason: Maintains aerobic stimulus without decoupling risk (target HR range avoids crossing into Z3 where TE spikes); shorter intervals prevent fatigue accumulation seen in recent 10.7 km effort.

risk_flags.evidence: Z4 % up 27%, aerobic TE up +0.3, cadence down -8 spm, VO2max values stable (40–42) but efficiency worsening — classic signs of functional overreaching before performance decline
risk_flags.action: Reduce Z4 exposure to ≤10% next week and restore Z1 to ≥40%

risk_flags.evidence: Vertical oscillation increased from 6.6 (8/23) to 8.4 (9/17), ground contact rose from 282 ms (9/3) to 327 ms (9/6), and stride length became more variable (74–102 cm across recent runs)
risk_flags.action: Prioritise cadence-focused drills and eliminate all speedwork until vertical oscillillation stabilises ≤7.5 and ground contact ≤305 ms

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from pace and intensity back to sustainable effort regulation, neuromuscular coordination, and autonomic recovery — using heart rate and cadence as real-time governors.
suggested_sessions: Z1/Z2 easy run with cadence focus
Short Z2 interval session with strict HR ceilings
